On top of DiLoCo, it introduces elastic aggregation, DARL, and queue-aware planning to provide the flexibility and resilience that batch-scheduled infrastructure requires. After 20,000 optimiser steps, the three-site run reaches a held-out perplexity of 34.7, against 28.2 for a centralised baseline. At H = 1000 H=1000 only 6% measured communication overhead. Data coverage held throughout: across four site departures in a three-site run, 1.2% of granted blocks were reclaimed and no block was lost or trained twice. The value of cross-site training today is therefore operational rather than competitive: it turns fragmented allocations into one training run, at an overhead we can quantify. Limitations . This was a proof of concept at a single small model scale, one epoch, and one site topology, without downstream benchmarking. Future work should test production-scale training across more facilities, with stronger fault tolerance and a planner informed by historical queue traces rather than only live probes.
